This is in fact a reproof, for no believer may make unlawful for himself what Allah has made lawful. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had not, by way of law and Shariah, made unlawful the honey or going to Mariyah. He had only resolved about himself that he would not do that act again. Upon this came this rebuke: that it is not permissible, for the sake of pleasing anyone, to deprive oneself of the things Allah has made lawful. From this the following conclusion is drawn.

﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (66:1): This indicates that the act is liable to be called to account, and its remedy is that forgiveness of Allah be sought and that Allah's mercy encompass one. This is an extremely subtle indication.

As for the oath to which the Qur'an is referring, which the Messenger of Allah had taken that he would not do it again, Allah said: come out of that oath, that is, by paying the expiation (kaffarah). And if an oath is taken to abstain from some good act, then breaking it and paying expiation for it is obligatory.

﴿And Allah is your Protector (Mawla)﴾ (66:2): Allah helps you in your weaknesses, and He helps you even in the matter that is burdensome for you. And this is why Allah has prescribed the method of making oaths lawful and coming out of them by paying expiation.

﴿And He is the All-Knowing, the All-Wise﴾ (66:2): He lays down for you the laws that He makes with knowledge and wisdom. And the commands He gives you are such that you can act upon them and they are beneficial for you. Therefore, make unlawful only those things that Allah has made unlawful, and do not make unlawful those things that Allah has made lawful. This is the fitting conclusion.

After this, the address turns to the matter which he (ﷺ) had stated, but its details are not related, because the matter itself was not so important, nor was it such a matter whose historical record needed to be preserved until the Day of Judgment. The only thing intended to be preserved was the effects and results of that matter.

﴿And when the Prophet confided to one of his wives a statement...﴾ (66:3)

(And this matter also deserves attention:) the Prophet confided a matter to one of his wives in secret.

It was a strange age, in which even in people's everyday lives there was open intervention from the higher realm. It became clear that Allah informed the Prophet ﷺ that the secret entrusted to one wife, with the strict instruction that no one else should learn of it, had been disclosed by her to another. When the Prophet ﷺ spoke to that wife who had kept the secret, he only hinted that she had not kept the secret as a secret. He did not give the full details of what she had told the other wife. This was the demand of his noble character (makarim al-akhlaq), that no one should be made to feel excessively ashamed. He let her know that news had come to him from the higher realm.

﴿Then when she disclosed it, and Allah informed him of it, he made known part of it and ignored part. Then when he told her of it, she said, "Who informed you of this?" He said, "I was informed by the All-Knowing, All-Aware."﴾ (66:3)

Since this news had spread because of the alliance between the two wives, a mere hint was enough to shame the wife who had spread it. In such situations, it is very necessary to point to Allah's knowledge and His awareness, because such a mistake occurs only when a person becomes heedless of, or forgets, Allah's knowledge and watchfulness. Therefore the Qur'an warns the Muslims that your follies are, in any case, within Allah's knowledge.

Now the discussion shifts from the third person to direct address, and the two wives who had done this are addressed directly, as though the matter is being spoken to them face to face.

﴿If you two turn to Allah in repentance, (it is better for you), for your hearts have deviated. And if you back each other against the Prophet, then know that Allah is his Protector, and after him Jibril, and the righteous believers, and the angels are his supporters.﴾ (66:4)

At the outset of the address they are invited to repent, so that their hearts may turn back toward Allah, since their hearts had strayed from Him. Once this invitation is given, a severe rebuke follows, delivered in a very stern tone.

This strong rebuke shows that, whatever the incident was, it had a deep effect on the blessed heart of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Accordingly, Allah had to declare that Allah, the angels, and the righteous believers are sufficient supporters for him. With this declaration, the Prophet's (ﷺ) distress is removed and he is reassured.

It appears that, whatever the incident was, it had a profound effect on the Prophet (ﷺ). He did not expect such an atmosphere within his own household. This is why the Ansari neighbour of Hazrat Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), in reporting this incident, described it as so dreadful that, by his account, it had become a greater matter than the attack of the Ghassanids. The Ghassanids then ruled Syria, and they were clients of the Roman Empire, and they had treaties of friendship with them. In that period, an attack on Madinah by the Ghassanids was a very dangerous matter. Yet for the Muslims, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) being troubled and restless was a greater matter than the attack of the Ghassanids. The security of the Prophet's (ﷺ) household was the greatest concern, and his distress was unbearable for people. This shows the perspective from which these people of the best generations (khayr al-qurun, the best of generations) viewed matters. Just as that Ansari regarded this incident as a grave matter, so Allah also regarded it in the same way. These companions' way of thinking had aligned itself with the direction of the thinking of Allah and His Messenger.

Then, in the next verse, they were told with great clarity what kind of women are fitting for the Prophet ﷺ and for his household. If he were to divorce you, his Lord could give him in your place wives better than you, who possess these qualities:

﴿Perhaps his Lord, if he divorces you, will give him in exchange wives better than you, who are submissive, faithful, obedient, repentant, devout, given to fasting, previously married and virgins.﴾ (66:5)

That is, you are being indirectly told how you ought to be: you should be true Muslims, obedient, and upholders of the commands of the religion. Your faith should be such that it fills the vessel of the heart with faith and certainty, and you should obey God and His Messenger from the heart. And repent, which means to feel remorse for what has happened and to become obedient from now on; remain constantly engaged in worship. "Sayahat" (wandering, fasting) and "sa'ihat" (those who travel in devotion) mean that one should continually reflect on God's greatness and majesty. Along with these qualities, they will be both previously married and virgins, just as the present wives of the Prophet ﷺ include both kinds of women.

This was a severe and powerful disciplinary rebuke to them for their faction-building against the Messenger of God ﷺ. It should be remembered that the Messenger of God ﷺ did not become angry over trivial matters.

With the revelation of these verses, the Prophet ﷺ was consoled. The Lord Himself addressed him and his household directly. After this tremor, there was deep regret within the household as well, and after God's guidance everything was set right. It was a great honour for this family that Almighty God Himself addressed it, for this was no ordinary household; every word of it became a manhaj (methodology) of life for those who came after, a code of conduct and a law.

These were the domestic circumstances of the one who was training a nation, laying the foundation of a state, and this state had no parallel in past history. No system like it existed among earlier nations. A nation was being formed which was presenting the divine vision of life in its final form. A Divine society was being brought into existence, and a society that was becoming a model for all time until the Day of Resurrection.

Then, in these verses, there is a portrait of a great, exalted, high-minded and generous human being. At one and the same time, he was fulfilling his human role and his prophetic role. No one can set a borderline between the two, because God's decree was that all the Messengers would be human beings. And this human Messenger was to bestow upon humanity the final system of life, which was to become the methodology of humanity until the Day of Resurrection.

This was a perfect message, brought by a perfect Messenger. And its perfection lay in this: that this message was making man truly human. It was not suppressing any of the human faculties, nor neglecting any of the constructive powers of man. Crushing any human capacity was not the purpose of this message; rather, it made human powers more refined, more trained and more elevated. This was the final message.

Those who understood Islam and moulded themselves in its mould, Islam adorned them in such a way that they became the true edition of Islam. Likewise, the Prophet's ﷺ biography and his practical life, which included human experiences, human striving, human weaknesses and human powers, together with the Quranic call and guidance, advanced these people step by step. In the same way, his household and those people's lives became a model for those who would come until the Day of Resurrection, but only for those who wish to see it, who live in the practical world, and who are not confined within their own shells and the narrow circles of their own ideas, and who have not closed their eyes.

By sending down this final message in its complete and perfect form, the Divine power gave it practical form in the life of a Messenger who took this message from heaven and translated it into living reality. Thus the Divine power made the life of this Messenger of the last age an open book, so that coming generations might take from his life the finest example and model.

In light of the incident that had a profound effect on the lives of the Muslims, the Qur'an now instructs the believers to protect themselves, their families and their households from the Fire. Thus a very impressive scene of the Day of Resurrection is also placed before them, showing the condition of the disbelievers there. Just as in that incident the wives were invited to repentance, so here the believers are invited to repent, and the gardens that Allah has prepared for those who repent are also described, and a glimpse of them is shown. And the Prophet (ﷺ) is told to wage jihad against the disbelievers and the hypocrites. This is the second paragraph of this surah:

﴿O you who believe! Save yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is men and stones, over which are angels stern and severe, who do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and who do what they are commanded.﴾ (66:6)

Upon the believer rests a great responsibility regarding his own self and his family. The Fire of the Day of Resurrection exists, and he must save himself and his household from it. It is a fire that blazes fiercely.

﴿Whose fuel is men and stones﴾ (66:6): people will be in it just as stones lie scattered, and no one will pay them any attention, like a stone on the road. How severe will that Fire be, that stones burn in it, how severe will the punishment be, and how worthless will the people of Hell be. The entire environment of Hell will be extremely intense and frightening.

﴿Over which are angels stern and severe﴾ (66:6): their temperament will be as harsh as the severity of that punishment.

﴿Who do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and do what they are commanded﴾ (66:6): their distinguishing feature is that they obey Allah, and their distinguishing feature is that whatever command is given to them, they carry it out. And because of this strength and firmness they have been appointed over that Fire. Therefore it is the duty of every believer to place barriers between himself, his self, his religion, his family and the Fire, before the moments of opportunity come to an end.

Look, when the disbelievers reach its mouth, they will offer excuses, but no excuse will be heard; rather, they will be utterly despairing there, when all their excuses are rejected.

"O you who disbelieve! Do not offer excuses today. You are being repaid only for what you used to do" (66:7). Do not offer excuses today, for today is not a day of excuses. Today everyone is receiving the fruit of what they did. And you well know what it is that you are receiving the fruit of today?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 66, verse 8:

The question is how believers can protect themselves and their families from that Fire. They are shown the way and given hope:

﴿O you who believe! Turn to Allah in sincere repentance (tawbah nasuh). It may be that your Lord will remove from you your evil deeds and admit you into Gardens beneath which rivers flow, on the Day when Allah will not disgrace the Prophet and those who believed along with him. Their light will run before them and on their right; they will say, "Our Lord, perfect for us our light and forgive us. Indeed, You are over all things competent."﴾ (66:8)

This is the method of sincere repentance: a repentance that purifies the heart, after which no deception remains. Repentance from sins happens when a person feels remorse for the sins he has committed, and that remorse then takes the place of those sins. This repentance purifies the heart, and the colour or rust of sinfulness upon it is removed. After this, the heart itself inclines a person toward righteous action. This is what is called tawbat al-nasuh (sincere repentance), that is, a repentance which keeps reminding the heart and does not allow it to commit sins again (constant admonition).

If someone makes this kind of repentance, then after it one may hope that earlier sins will also be forgiven because of it, and the penitent will enter the Gardens. On that day the disbelievers will be deeply humiliated, while the Prophet ﷺ and the believers will not be humiliated.

Here Allah has joined the believers with the Prophet ﷺ in order to motivate them to repentance, saying: "Look, on that day you will be encouraged to such an extent that you will stand in the row of the Prophet ﷺ, you will be honoured, and you will not be disgraced. And on that day a light will go before you."

﴿Their light will run before them and on their right﴾ (66:8). On that day they will be recognised by this light. That day will be very frightening, stormy and heart-shaking, in which there will be crowding on every side, and they will have the honour that, at the time of entering Paradise, a light will go before them and on their right. With this light they will go into Paradise, where there will be light upon light.

Although the believers will be in that severe and frightening place, they will have the courage to present this supplication and petition before Allah:

﴿They will say, "Our Lord, perfect for us our light and forgive us. Indeed, You are over all things competent."﴾ (66:8) At a time when tongues are silent and hearts are sinking, teaching the believers such a supplication in that dreadful situation is itself a sign that it will be accepted. It has been taught precisely so that it may be accepted, because Allah is teaching them this supplication as a favour, just as the light will be running for their honour.

That punishment and that reward in fact define the responsibility of a believer: how great a responsibility rests upon the believer for protecting himself and his family. Especially since these instructions are being given in connection with an event that took place in the household of the Prophet ﷺ, a believer is responsible for the guidance and upbringing of his family. Just as he is obliged to reform himself, he is also obliged to reform his household and dependants.

It should be remembered that Islam is a family-based system, as we said in Surah al-Talaq: the believer bears responsibility for reforming his household. For a believing household is the first cell of the Islamic community, and from these cells living cells are then produced within the Islamic community. Every house is a circle or bastion of the Islamic worldview. This circle must be very strong in its structure, and every member of it must be engaged in defence at the frontiers. If this bastion is not strong, the enemy will enter within and no defence will be possible.

The believing dai has the duty to begin his call from his own home. The fortress must be strong from within, and before going out of this fortress he must close every breach in the inner fortress. A household can be protected only if the mother too is a Muslim; the father alone cannot guard this fortress. Mother and father together can set boys and girls right, because if anyone says that he wants to build an Islamic society with men alone, this is not possible. The Islamic revolution needs believing women too, so that they may raise the coming generation along Islamic lines.

This is why the Qur'an, just as it was revealed for men, was revealed for women as well. It was organising households alongside organising men; it was establishing households upon the Islamic method. Therefore it placed upon a Muslim the responsibility for his own religious guidance and the guidance of his family.

﴿O you who believe! Protect yourselves and your families from a Fire﴾ (66:6)

This is the point which those who call people to Islam must understand well. The work of reform should begin with one's wife, then move to the mother, then to the children, and then to all relatives. Every effort should be made that we bring into being a Muslim woman, from whom Muslims are born. Whoever wishes to build a Muslim household must first seek out a Muslim woman. If we fail to produce a Muslim mistress of the household, then let it be remembered that the formation of the Islamic community and Islamic society will take a long time, and there will be weaknesses within the foundations and bases of our community.

In the first Islamic community this work was very easy, because in Medina an Islamic society had come into being; pure ideas dominated society. The Shari'ah was being implemented alongside it, and men and women all brought their matters to Allah and His Messenger, listened to the command of Allah and of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and when a command was revealed it was the final decision. At that time the Islamic society existed, was dominant, and in those circumstances it was easy for a woman to shape herself along Islamic lines. It was also easy for husbands to counsel them and to raise the children.

But we are in utterly changed circumstances. We live within a completely Jahili society. The law that prevails is Jahili; morality is Jahili; knowledge and culture are Jahili. And today a woman too works within this Jahili society. Today, when a woman even intends to answer the call of Islam, she feels a very great burden in it, whether she herself wishes to move towards Islam or her husband and father instruct her to move towards it.

In the first generation, men, women and society were all under one conception. They were governed by Islam; the form was one, and Islam was present and in force in practice. Today the condition of the believing man is that he wants the rule of an imagined conception which in practice does not exist, while society in practice is a Jahili society. The pressure of this society falls more heavily on the woman than on the man. Modern society is misguiding women very rapidly.

At this point the responsibility of the man becomes much greater. He has to protect himself and also protect his family, in circumstances where wife and children are surrounded by an environment in which Jahili assault comes at them from every side.

Therefore today's Muslim must clearly understand that for reform he will have to strive thousands of times harder than the community of the first generation. So whoever wishes to build an Islamic fortress in this age has the duty, before intending to build such a house, to seek for himself a guardian of this fortress whose thoughts and convictions are the same as his own. In this matter a revolutionary husband will have to make some sacrifices. The first sacrifice will be that he does not seek beauty, does not seek wealth, and is not pleased by false embellishment. He should seek a religious woman who, together with him, forms a Muslim household and builds a Muslim fortress. And fathers of children also have the duty to attend to their children and dependants, and not to call others before first attending to their sons, daughters and grandchildren. And they should act upon what Allah is calling out loud.

﴿O you who believe! Protect yourselves and your families from a Fire﴾ (66:6)

Once again I come to this point: Islam wishes to build a society over which Islam rules, within which Islam truly exists. Its method, which Islam has adopted, is a community whose creed is Islam, whose system is Islam, whose law is Islamic, whose way of life is Islamic, and which takes all its conceptions from the teachings of Islam.

The treasury of the Islamic conception of life is this community. It is its guardian, and it transmits it to others. And against every kind of Jahili pressure it defends it, and it protects this community from that harm.

Therefore the establishment of an Islamic community or Islamic society is necessary, within which a Muslim woman may live and not be affected or pressured by the Jahiliyyah of her environment. In this way she will emerge from the struggle between Islamic requirements and the demands of Jahiliyyah. In such circumstances, if a young Muslim man and this Muslim woman together build an Islamic fortress, then from such fortresses an Islamic bloc and Islamic front can be formed.

This is a necessity and a duty, not merely optional, that an Islamic society be established which mutually counsels one another toward truth and Islam, nourishes its thought, practically puts its morals and manners into action, and whose members live among one another in an Islamic colour: alive for Islam, guardians of Islam, callers to Islam. And among the people of Jahiliyyah whom they invite to their society, let them see that within this community and society there is a living Islam, so that they may come out from darkness into light by the command of Allah. And let this society keep growing, so that Allah brings about an Islamic revolution, and then future generations, raised under this community and its training, are prepared in the colour of the Islamic revolution.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 66, verse 9:

In Medina, the Muslims had built exactly such a community and had brought about exactly such a revolution. Therefore, guidance is given here for its protection, because the disbelievers and the hypocrites wished to destroy it.

﴿O Prophet! Strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be stern with them. Their abode is Hell, and it is an evil destination﴾ (66:9). First, the command was given that the Muslims should save themselves and their families from Hell, and make sincere repentance (tawbah nasuh), through which their sins would be forgiven, and they would enter gardens beneath which rivers flow. Now the command is to wage war against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, because they are alarmed by the establishment of this kind of Islamic society, in which devotees of Islam are prepared. They attack such a society, just as in Medina the aim of the disbelievers and the hypocrites was this, and it is this today, and it will be this in the future.

Here, both the disbelievers and the hypocrites are commanded to be subjected to jihad and sternness, because both have the same aims for the demolition of the Islamic society. Therefore, both require sternness.

﴿And their abode is Hell, and it is an evil destination﴾ (66:9). Thus a connection is established between these two matters.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 66, verse 10:

Now comes the third section. This is the final section of this surah, and this third section also completes the previous one. It speaks of disbelieving women in the houses of prophets, and of believing women in the houses of disbelievers.

ضرب اللہ ................................ من القنتین
[Allah sets forth an example... among the obedient (al-qanitin)]

Regarding the wives of Prophet Nuh (peace be upon him) and Prophet Lut (peace be upon him), the statement that they betrayed their husbands means that they acted against their husbands' call (da'wah). It does not mean that they committed any immorality. The wife of Nuh (peace be upon him) used to mock her husband along with the other mockers. And the wife of Lut (peace be upon him) informed the wicked men about his guests, although she knew that Lut (peace be upon him) opposed that abomination.

Concerning the wife of Pharaoh, it is related that she was a believer. Perhaps she was an Asiatic and followed the religion of Musa (peace be upon him). History records that the mother of the Egyptian king Amenhotep IV was Asiatic, and she did not follow the religion of the Egyptians. This was the same king who devised for the Egyptians a single god and made the disc of the sun its symbol, and he gave himself the title Akhenaten. In any case, either this woman is meant, or the wife of the Pharaoh who was contemporary with Musa (peace be upon him) is meant. The Pharaoh of Musa (peace be upon him) was not Amenhotep.

Here we do not need historical research into Pharaoh's wife. What the Qur'an has indicated is sufficient. Names and persons are examples for principles, and the Qur'an often omits names and persons. After commanding that you strive to save yourselves and your families, this principle is nonetheless repeated: every person is responsible for his own deeds. The wives of the Prophet's household and the wives of the believers are told: be mindful of your own end; no one will be spared merely because he is the son of a prophet, or the wife of a prophet, or the son or wife of a righteous person.

Just look at the wives of Nuh (peace be upon him) and Lut (peace be upon him).

"كانتا ........................ الداخلين" (66:10) "They were under two of Our righteous servants, but they betrayed them, and the two husbands could not avail them at all against Allah. It was said to them both: enter the Fire along with those who enter it." In the matter of disbelief, there is no one greater or lesser, and no intercession works between disbelief and faith. If anyone betrays the Islamic way of life, even if she is the wife of a prophet, she will be thrown into Hell.

Behold the wife of Pharaoh: the storm of disbelief did not affect her, though she was living within that storm, in Pharaoh's palace. She sought deliverance from it, and desired a palace in Paradise rather than the contemptible Pharaoh's. She was not with Pharaoh's disbelief; she was seeking deliverance from it, and her wishes were these:

﴿When she said: "My Lord! Build for me, near You, a house in Paradise, and save me from Pharaoh and his deeds, and save me from the wrongdoing people."﴾ (66:11)

The supplication of Pharaoh's believing wife is an example of how, when faith becomes firmly rooted, a believing woman spurns the highest worldly life. Pharaoh of Egypt was counted, in his era, among the great kings of the world. And within Pharaoh's palace, a woman obtains the most exalted provisions. Yet through faith she soars higher than even that. She does not regard it as luxury but as filth, and she seeks refuge from that life and wishes to be delivered from it.

She is the first lady of a most magnificent kingdom. And this is her great distinguishing quality, for a woman always yields to social pressure and influence, but this lone woman stands firm against that tremendous pressure. Upon her is the pressure of society, the pressure of the palace, the pressure of the kingdom, the pressure of the king's ministers and courtiers, and the pressure of the status of being the king's queen. Yet against this all-encompassing pressure, this great woman holds her head high towards the sky, and sits within that vast ocean of disbelief upon a small plank, and her hem is not soaked by all those defilements. How magnificent she is!!

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 66, verse 12:

This is an extremely elevated example of being wholly devoted to Allah, for she confronted every influence, every relationship, and overcame every obstacle. For this reason her name has been inscribed in the everlasting Book of Allah. And when this Book is revealed, her name will be called out, and its echo will resonate through the boundless valleys of this vast universe.

﴿And Mary, daughter of 'Imran﴾ (66:21). She too was a chaste woman from the very beginning. The Qur'an praises her in other surahs; here the subject is the nobility of her character and her purity.

﴿Who guarded her chastity﴾ (66:21). The Jews made accusations against her, and the Qur'an declares her innocence.

﴿Then We breathed into her of Our Spirit﴾ (66:21). And through that Spirit, Hadrat 'Isa (peace be upon him) was born, as the details have passed in Surah Maryam. There is no need to repeat them here, because the purpose here is only to establish her purity and her perfect faith.

﴿And she accepted the words of her Lord and His scriptures, and she was among the obedient﴾ (66:21).

The separate mention of the wife of Pharaoh here, and then placing her on the same level as Hadrat Maryam (peace be upon her), is evidence that the rank of Pharaoh's wife was also very high in the sight of Allah, because she remained steadfast upon the path of faith in extremely difficult circumstances. In any case, these two examples are placed before the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ), so that you may understand that your conduct should be this elevated, and the believers are told until the Day of Resurrection that if they wish to establish an Islamic society, they must produce women of character and Muslim women.

In conclusion, we again draw the attention of readers to the fact that this surah and this entire part are an excellent and living example of the Sirah of the Prophet (ﷺ). These surahs show that the community of Companions, men and women, which the Prophet (ﷺ) trained, has no parallel in human history. Moreover, the manner in which the Qur'an narrates the events of the Sirah of the Prophet (ﷺ) is a unique style of the Qur'an. By taking a particular incident out of its specific circumstances and stripping it of the colour of time and place, the Qur'an presents it as an eternal principle. Only the Qur'an can do this. The reader reads and understands it against the background of a particular event, but the conclusions that the Qur'an draws from it are universal.
